creep_sustained_fraction_is_SUPERSEDED: READ THIS BEFORE USING creep_sustained_fraction. It is a time-blind blanket rule ('sustained = 20-30% of yield') derived from the very static yield a creep check exists to replace, and it is NOT an allowable. Where a material record in tools/materials/<key>.json carries a `creep` block, that TEMPERATURE x DURATION TABLE GOVERNS (OPERATOR_BRIEF §7, and the record's own `conflicts` ledger). PLA: this file's 55.0 x 0.2 = 11.0 MPa versus the table's 5.0 MPa at 23 C / 24 h and 2.5 MPa at 23 C / 1 y — up to 4.4x optimistic. The ONE reader of that table is tools/materials.py (`creep_lookup` / `creep_allowable_mpa`), mirrored bit-for-bit by kernel_model::materials::pla and pinned by tools/materials/creep_crosslang_vectors.json. tools/production_check.py reads the table at a STATED service temperature and duration and REFUSES rather than falling back to this fraction; only PLA has a table, so every other material here REFUSES a sustained-load verdict outright. The fraction stays in this file only so the conflict remains visible.
disclaimer: typical desktop-FDM values — verify per filament brand. Yield/ultimate/modulus are as-printed XY (flat-on-bed) datasheet-class numbers; layer_adhesion_factor scales them for across-layer (Z) loading; creep_sustained_fraction and fatigue_knockdown are engineering rules of thumb (sustained-load allowable fraction of yield; ~1e6-cycle allowable fraction of ultimate), not measured filament data.

PLA.source: typical of Prusament/Ultimaker PLA datasheets (tensile 50-60 MPa, E 2.9-3.6 GPa, HDT-B 55-60 C). Creep fraction set LOW (0.2): PLA cold-flows measurably at room temperature under sustained load.

PETG.source: typical of Prusament/Ultimaker PETG datasheets (tensile 47-50 MPa, E 1.5-2.1 GPa, HDT-B 70-78 C); PETG has among the best layer adhesion of the commodity filaments.

ABS.source: typical printed-ABS datasheets (tensile 30-44 MPa, E 1.8-2.4 GPa, HDT-B 95-100 C); layer adhesion suffers without an enclosure — 0.5 assumes a decent chamber.

ASA.source: typical ASA datasheets (Prusament ASA tensile ~45 MPa, HDT-B ~93 C); ABS-like with better UV stability and slightly better layer bonding.

TPU95A.source: Ultimaker TPU 95A datasheet (E 26 MPa, yield 8.6 MPa, break 39 MPa at ~580% elongation) — moduli of 95A TPUs vary WIDELY (26-90 MPa) between brands; elastomers bond layers well (0.75) and tolerate cyclic strain (0.4) but cold-flow under sustained load (0.2).

PC.source: typical printed-PC datasheets (Prusament PC Blend tensile ~63 MPa, HDT-B ~113 C); strong but notoriously poor layer adhesion without a hot chamber — 0.45.

PA.source: typical printed-nylon (PA6/PA12 blends, e.g. Polymaker PA6-CF matrix / Taulman) DRY-as-printed values; moisture conditioning can HALVE yield and modulus — treat these as dry-part numbers and verify conditioned.
